name: Powada (Marathi heroic-ballad)
lineage: Powada Marathi heroic-ballad tradition of Maharashtra, celebrating military and historical-political figures through declamatory narrative-and-call-and-response song. The canonical core centers on the seventeenth-century Maratha-Empire founder Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj — the powada of Tanaji Malusare's heroic death at the 1670 Battle of Sinhagad is most internationally circulated. Performance: male lead-singer-narrator (shahir) with chorus and dholak percussion, vigorous declamatory delivery, and audience call-and-response. The shahir is historically a respected community-poet-historian; nineteenth-century social-reformer Jyotirao Phule used powada for political consciousness-raising.
